dimensions.note: Nominal size from the size code; no datasheet was fetched for this size. Unprotected battery. Protected batteries (with a circuit board) and button-top batteries are longer than the bare flat-top battery, commonly by 2 to 5mm; check the maker's listed length before relying on a fit.

variants.notes: Nominal voltage 3.7V. One protected 14650 is listed at 1100mAh and 3.7V nominal.

safety: Charge only with a charger made for lithium-ion batteries, using constant current then constant voltage (CC/CV) up to the charge voltage in the battery datasheet (4.2V for cobalt, nickel and manganese chemistries, 3.65V for lithium iron phosphate).
Do not discharge below the datasheet cutoff voltage (2.5V for most batteries listed here); deep discharge damages the battery and a damaged battery should be discarded.
The metal can is the negative terminal. A torn or missing wrap exposes the can and can short the battery against a metal object or an adjacent battery.

Unprotected batteries have no overcharge, over-discharge or short-circuit protection of their own and need protection in the charger or the device; protected batteries carry a circuit board but should still be charged with a matching charger.

Transport limits apply: the U.S. FAA requires spare lithium-ion batteries to travel in carry-on baggage with the terminals protected against short circuit, and limits rechargeable lithium-ion batteries to 100Wh each (FAA PackSafe).
